arxiv-2310-06305.title: On the mass transfer in the 3D Pitaevskii model
arxiv-2310-06305.creator: Juhi Jang, Pranava Chaitanya Jayanti, Igor Kukavica
arxiv-2310-06305.description: Abstract . We examine a micro-scale model of superfluidity derived by Pitaevskii [ Pit59 ] which describes the interacting dynamics between superfluid He-4 and its normal fluid phase. This system consists of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation and the incompressible, inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations, coupled to each other via a bidirectional nonlinear relaxation mechanism.

arxiv-2404-08725.description: Abstract Neutrinos from very nearby supernovae, such as Betelgeuse, are expected to generate more than ten million events over 10 s in Super-Kamokande (SK). At such large event rates, the buffers of the SK analog-to-digital conversion board (QBEE) will overflow, causing random loss of data that is critical for understanding the dynamics of the supernova explosion mechanism.

arxiv-2408-03579.title: “The Strength of Weak Ties” Varies Across Viral Channels Thanks: Thanks to Yifan Yu and Haojun Wu for helpful discussion and support.
arxiv-2408-03579.creator: Shan Huang, Yuan Yuan, University of California, Davis, Yi Ji
arxiv-2408-03579.description: Abstract The diffusion of novel information through social networks is essential for dismantling echo chambers and promoting innovation. Our study examines how two major types of viral channels, specifically Direct Messaging (DM) and Broadcasting (BC), impact the well-known “strength of weak ties” in disseminating novel information across social networks.

arxiv-2505-08390.title: Engineering long-range and multi-body interactions via global kinetic constraints
arxiv-2505-08390.creator: Runmin Wu, Bing Yang, Pieter W. Claeys, Hongzheng Zhao
arxiv-2505-08390.description: Abstract Long-range and multi-body interactions are crucial for quantum simulation and quantum computation. Yet, their practical realization using elementary pairwise interactions remains an outstanding challenge. We propose an experimental scheme based on the Bose-Hubbard system with a periodic driving of the on-site energy and global-range density-density interactions, a setup readily implementable via cold atoms in optical lattices with cavity-mediated interactions.

pmc-11331035.title: The dual role of cellular senescence in human tumor progression and therapy
pmc-11331035.creator: Liang Ma, Jie Yu, Yidian Fu, Xiaoyu He, Shengfang Ge, Renbing Jia, Ai Zhuang, Zhi Yang, Xianqun Fan
pmc-11331035.description: Cellular senescence, one of the hallmarks of cancer, is characterized by cell cycle arrest and the loss of most normal cellular functions while acquiring a hypersecretory, proinflammatory phenotype. The function of senescent cells in cancer cells varies depending on the cellular conditions. Before the occurrence of cancer, senescent cells act as a barrier to prevent its development.

pmc-12608611.title: Study on the γ/γ′ Eutectic Inhomogeneity of a Novel 3rd Generation Nickel-Based Single-Crystal Superalloy Casting
pmc-12608611.creator: Xiaoshan Liu, Anping Long, Haijie Zhang, Dexin Ma, Min Song, Menghuai Wu, Jianzheng Guo, Gábor Harsányi
pmc-12608611.description: In the manufacture of single-crystal blades for aero-engines, the problem of eutectic aggregation on the upper surface of the blades has long been restricting the casting performance improvement. To investigate this phenomenon, this paper employs a simplified blade-like shape casting and focuses a 3rd generation nickel-based single-crystal superalloy as the research material.

pmc-12754598.title: ﻿Mazama tschudii (Wagner, 1855), forgotten by science, re-emerges as a new genetic lineage of Neotropical deer with a proposed neotype (Artiodactyla, Cervidae)
pmc-12754598.creator: Eluzai Dinai Pinto Sandoval, José Eduard Hernández-Guevara, Agda Maria Bernegossi, Pedro Henrique Faria Peres, Renato Caparroz, José Maurício Barbanti Duarte
pmc-12754598.description: ﻿AbstractThe accurate classification of Neotropical deer is essential for effective conservation strategies; however, many species within the genus Mazama remain taxonomically unresolved due to morphological similarities and historical uncertainties. Mazama tschudii, originally described from the western Andes of Peru, has been debated due to the absence of a designated type specimen and its resemblance to other brocket species.

pmc-13282919.title: Bond and Antibond Resonances: A Unified Framework for Singlet Biradical Character
pmc-13282919.creator: Daniel T. Gschwind, Jonas Bresien
pmc-13282919.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). While the mathematical description of the electronic structure of biradical(oid)s is nowadays well understood, we feel that the chemical‐conceptual understanding of the structure and bonding, especially of singlet biradicaloids, remains underdeveloped. In particular, the degree of “biradical character” of singlet biradicaloids is discussed in the literature using a heterogeneous selection of indices, which are often not directly comparable and therefore hamper the development of a systematic understanding as well as comparison of different biradicaloid species.
